reviewer: Implementing Codex agent, unblinded; no traveller or mentor ratings collected
scope: All ten completed answers read against their exact request context. Original outputs were not repaired.

cases.finding: Proposes all five with experience estimates; weather remains unavailable and light references null. Durations are suggestions, not operator rules or actual dwell-time evidence.
Reading and coffee ranges both shorten following the explicit wish. This demonstrates responsiveness, not empirical accuracy or a universal duration standard.
Selects morning opportunity for the photo main spot and explicitly states the weather samples do not cover that solar window. Weather advice is cautious and somewhat generic.

Describes the changed rain/cloud regime without replacing places or asserting certainty. Uses malam for source period evening, whose actual sample is 17:00-18:00 local: terminology/time-period ambiguity requiring normalization.

Correctly distinguishes low rain from high cloud and preserves the calculated solar opportunity. Reading duration grows despite an unchanged deep-reading wish; variation is not justified by verified operator facts.

No solar window selected and light priority becomes not_relevant when photography is deprioritized. Calls a synthetic forecast amount curah tercatat, an avoidable observation-like wording. Park remains role main because its input anchor was unchanged, creating tension with prose prioritizing reading/food.
Retains calculated light opportunity while explicitly leaving weather unknown. No fabricated clear-sky or dry-weather claim.

No invented indoor seating or shelter; unknown market/library activity durations are null with reasons. Conditional reading at the cafe is explicitly contingent on appropriate seating; it is not asserted as a facility fact.

Uses fictional supplied outdoor/photo attributes only for the fictional parks. Proposes morning A and evening B with an alternative order and no promise that both windows can be reached. Because both morning/evening options were supplied, this is not a forced same-window impossibility test.

Exact request repeats the order but not all estimated ranges: market max changes 75 to 90, coffee changes 45-75 to 40-70, library daypart changes flexible to afternoon. Exact deterministic estimates or dayparts are not established.

requiredBeforeProductUse: Normalize daypart labels against explicit local-time intervals; do not let evening ambiguously imply night.
Use forecast language such as diprakirakan, not wording suggesting observed future rainfall.
Keep duration ranges labelled estimates and decide how proposal persistence/regeneration should handle variation.
Define how main-spot anchoring interacts with a later changed activity priority.
Reduce repeated warnings without removing material uncertainties.
Obtain human evaluation and real-source integration evidence; neither is completed by this experiment.
acceptance: Bounded model capability demonstrated; production, empirical-duration, road/timing and real-weather acceptance not established.
